memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure whether retaining row packing in the fused path changes that interaction.

proposal.hypothesis: Row-packing the shared-staged fused forward/input-gradient kernel may avoid the extra time observed when fusion replaced Gm2’s packed passes, while preserving its four-j weight-gradient kernel. Shared-memory and fusion overhead may still outweigh the saved launch; only full-call measurement can decide.

retained: Fuse forward and input-gradient computation into one kernel while packing rows per CTA using the Gm2 mapping; retain bounds-safe zero padding and fresh writes.

For shared-memory-sized cases, cooperatively stage each packed row’s x and gy halo and filter, using a zero-padded halo; use a global-memory bounds-checked fallback when the shared-memory requirement exceeds 8 KiB.
Retain Gm2’s four-adjacent-j FP32 weight-gradient CTA reduction and its complete gk writes; do not use uninitialized scratch.
